text:
maria: Heads-up — several nodes in the gpupool (us-west1) are flipping to NotReady and getting NoSchedule taints for GPUs. Spotted during a normal scale-up.
aj: seeing the same. autoscaler keeps launching nodes then they go NotReady within ~30s :grimacing:
sachin: from kubelet logs: repeated 'plugin reported: exit status 1' and kernel messages about device unbind. dmesg shows udev timeouts.
kevin: paste of 'kubectl get nodes' showing statuses:
```
NAME                                       STATUS                     ROLES   AGE   VERSION
gpupool-1-node-abc                         NotReady,SchedulingDisabled   <none>   4h    v1.27.3
gpupool-1-node-def                         NotReady,SchedulingDisabled   <none>   3h    v1.27.3
gpupool-1-node-ghi                         Ready                       <none>   5h    v1.27.3
```
maria: kubelet also logs: "failed to register device plugin: plugin crashed: exit status 1" — looks like the nvidia device plugin is crashing during init.
didi: @aj did we change the node image or kernel on that pool in last deploy window? region tag us-west1-b.
aj: we rolled the node kernel from 5.15.120 -> 5.15.122 overnight for security patches on that node-template.
sachin: suspecting a udev/module race with the new kernel + driver combo. dmesg excerpt:
```
[  12.345678] nvidia 0000:81:00.0: failed to unbind: device or resource busy
[  12.345679] udevd[1234]: worker [1235] /lib/udev/rules.d/60-nvidia.rules took too long
[  12.345680] nvidia: probe of 0000:81:00.0 failed with error -16
```
kevin: nodes get the taint `node.kubernetes.io/gpu-unavailable:NoSchedule` from our init hook. autoscaler sees NotReady and attempts replacement, which immediately fails too.
maria: autoscaler policy currently has a 0s stabilization for scale down; it's aggressively terminating fallback pools and causing on-demand fallback to spin up — cost spike already.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-7893 — "gpupool us-west1 NotReady after kernel roll".
aj: short-term mitigation options:
- roll back node-template to previous kernel image
- change cloud-init to modprobe nvidia early and ensure nvidia-modprobe preloads before kubelet
- cordon/taint new nodes to prevent scheduling until patch applied
sachin: also recommend adding a 10m stabilization window to the cluster-autoscaler for this gpupool to avoid thrash.
didi: I'll start a nodepool rollback to the previous image and hold further auto-rolls. pinging infra-sre for expedite.
kevin: note: us-west1 GPU quota is tight; if rollback doesn't work we might need to route jobs to us-central which increases latency for some customers.
maria: action items: rollback node image (didi), change autoscaler policy to add 10m stabilization (aj), collect full dmesg + lsmod + driver package list from failing nodes (sachin). I'll attach logs to INC-7893.
aj: ack — applying autoscaler tweak now :wrench:
sachin: saving current node debug tarball to /tmp/gpu-debug-2125012345.tar.gz and uploading to incident thread.
kevin: after rollback we should add a preflight check in our node-rolling job to validate nvidia modules load and device-plugin registration before marking image as production.
maria: thanks everyone — please update the incident with any new findings.
